images.title: Parallel lines, equal corners
images.purpose: Show that every pair of corresponding angles on parallel lines is equal: two pairs of 65° and two of 115°.
images.composition: Two clearly parallel lines and one transversal centred, two angle sizes shown by two colours.
exact_structure: Two horizontal parallel lines, l above and m below, each with two small arrow marks (>>) on the right end.
One slanting transversal t that rises to the right, crossing l and m.
At each crossing the angles are: upper right 65°, upper left 115°, lower left 65°, lower right 115°.
All four 65° angles filled teal (#0072B2); all four 115° angles filled amber (#E69F00).
So there are 8 filled angles, 4 teal and 4 amber, and matching corners at l and m have the same colour and number.
rejection: a 65° and 115° swapped between matching corners
missing arrow marks on the lines
not eight filled angles (four 65° and four 115°)
images.takeaway: On parallel lines matching corners always have the same size.
images.description: Parallel lines l and m crossed by a transversal, with matching corners coloured and labelled 65° or 115°.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students compare the colour of each corner at l with the same corner at m.

image_decisions.why: Colour makes the equal corresponding pairs visible at once.
